ai.description: *Cnemaspis flaviventralis* reaches 40 mm SVL. It features a dark brown dorsum with pale spots and a diagnostic bright yellow venter. A distinct white vertebral stripe and granular scales identify it.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis flaviventralis* is best distinguished by the vibrant, uniform yellow coloration on its venter, which contrasts sharply with the pale or mottled bellies of similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis flaviventralis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within moist deciduous forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis flaviventralis* is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks during the brightest hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis flaviventralis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two spherical eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis flaviventralis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu, India, typically inhabiting rocky areas at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
